transcript.text: the door on our built in dishwasher just crashes down when you open it now, used to stay put. Hotpoint I think

That 'crashing' sound usually means the mechanism that holds the door open has failed. In most dishwashers, this is caused by worn or broken balance springs (or cables) located at the top corners of the door hinge area. These wear out over time and lose their tension. To check this safely: please switch off the dishwasher at the wall socket first. Then look at the top inside edge of the open door. You should see two metal springs or cables connecting the door to the cabinet frame on either side. Are they both present, intact, and pulling tight when you lift the door slightly?

Ok. The left side still has a bit of tension but the right side has none. I can see a loose spring hanging down on the right when I shine a torch under the plinth. Heard a twang last week when it went.

That suggests the right-hand balance spring has detached or broken; that 'twang' was likely the metal snapping. To get you the correct replacement part for your Hotpoint, I need the model number. It’s usually on a sticker on the side edge of the door or inside the door frame—can you read it for me?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
The sticker on the door edge is partly peeled, but I can see it starts with LTF. I can't read the rest of it, sorry. I think it might be LTF 8B019 but I'm not sure.

That suggests it: the right-hand door balance spring has snapped or detached. Because the left side still has tension but the right doesn't, the door loses its counter-balance and crashes down. Since your model number is only partially visible (LTF 8B019), I recommend finding the full model number on a sticker inside the door frame or on the side of the door when it's open. You can then search for 'Hotpoint dishwasher door balance springs' using that full code to ensure you get the correct pair. Please switch off and unplug the dishwasher before attempting any repair. Replacing these springs usually involves removing the top hinge cover, detaching the old spring from the door and cabinet, and fitting the new one (often requiring a specific winding tool or technique). If you are not comfortable with this mechanical work, it is best to call an engineer.

Thanks. I can't slide the unit out to get at the hinge area, the fixing screws are hard to reach and the plinth is tight. Is there any way to sort it without pulling it out, or is an engineer the best bet?

[Heading: Likely cause: door hinge]
Given that you cannot pull the dishwasher out and the screws are difficult to reach through the plinth, this is best left to an engineer. Replacing door balance springs requires removing the top hinge cover and detaching the springs from both the door and the cabinet frame; doing this in a cramped space without pulling the unit out is very awkward and risks damaging the door or the hinges further. An engineer has the tools and experience to work around the plinth or safely move the appliance if needed.
